verdict.rationale: Auth0's docs confirm that social login is a first-party capability: users can sign in with social accounts such as Facebook or X, and Universal Login supports social, enterprise and custom identity providers. The evidence names only two providers, though, and never shows these providers being enabled through dashboard configuration rather than code, so breadth and the no-code part of the story are unproven. Missing for 10: a documented catalog of supported social/OAuth providers, explicit evidence that providers are turned on by configuration without custom code, and independent hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a developer, I can offer sign-in with a broad set of social and OAuth identity providers through configuration, not custom code

citations.quote: Your users should be able to log in either with an identifier (username, email, or phone number) and password or with their social accounts (such as Facebook or X).
supports a wide range of login methods, including username/password, social IDs, enterprise SSO, email/sms passwordless, biometrics via WebAuthN and Passkeys
